feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector alignment. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with impact occasionally diluted by long lists and limited outcome-focused metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing leadership, ownership, and strategic scope over time.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms, tools, and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack).  
- Writing is polished and consistent overall, with a strong executive positioning in the header and relevant recent project examples.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten style consistency: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” usage is fine but punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” instead. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and public-sector focus. It’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, so it would benefit from sharper positioning and fewer list-like phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and align it more closely with the subtitle: “Senior digital leader” + “12+ years” + public-sector specialization.
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with more direct, active phrasing.
- Emphasize highest-value themes from recent roles: enterprise web modernization, analytics, governance, and AI-enabled search/UX.
- Consider rewrite: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web, analytics, and editorial operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Leads digital governance, CMS and content workflow design, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and user experiences for complex, mission-driven teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and user experiences” is more specific.
- The subtitle already signals leadership, so avoid repeating too many broad capability labels here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into sharper, less repetitive capability areas with more consistent phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and shorten where possible: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations
- Replace broader items with more distinctive strengths: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider “web” instead of “website” for a cleaner, more executive tone.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “search and content experiences” vs. “operations” and “infrastructure.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid restating tools or channel details covered elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” may duplicate both the header and multiple NACo roles unless positioned as a distinct specialization.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an extension of the experience section and repeats themes already covered elsewhere. Tightening the wording and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and shorten each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action verbs and style: “Built,” “Developed,” “Launched,” “Produced.”
- Increase specificity where possible with scale, audience, or deliverables; e.g., “Drupal 10 microsite,” “interactive conference display,” “bill-level AI chat.”
- Refine wording for clarity: change “10×20-foot” to “10 x 20-foot” and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search and the microsite project overlap with the current freelance role; keep this block project-focused and avoid repeating strategy/governance language.
- Advocacy Video Series overlaps with NACo experience; highlight the program format or distribution model rather than restating production responsibilities.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads as a responsibility list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes, scale, or implementation status wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets and lead with the most distinctive work: AI-enabled search, Drupal campaign experiences, and organization-wide workflow/analytics systems.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, toolkit downloads, search improvements, workflow time saved, or reduction in support issues.
- Example rewrite: “Lead digital strategy and enterprise web improvement for a U.S. national membership organization, building Drupal-based campaign experiences, organization-wide content workflows, analytics systems, and an AI-enabled search initiative to improve content discovery and communications coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with NACo governance/workflow bullets; keep only if you can show a new scope or result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a concrete project or outcome.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational scope, and promotion-level progression without repeating responsibilities covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: growth in engagement, production savings from the studio, reporting efficiency, campaign performance, or governance adoption rates.
- Tighten channel bullet: combine audience and leadership scope, e.g., “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and other public-sector stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity.
- “Improved workflows/publishing consistency” repeats earlier NACo roles; here, frame it as enterprise governance and cross-department operating systems.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at the manager-to-director transition point.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Led NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize ownership and outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show channel-building impact: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video work also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep focus here on scaling/operationalizing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing that repeats elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, senior-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Editorial governance and publishing operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector and advocacy communications,” “Audience and content strategy.”
- Keep each line parallel and noun-based; avoid softer phrasing like “audience-focused content planning,” which reads less executive than the rest.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Editorial governance for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”
- Consider reducing to 4 lines to increase distinction and scannability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear almost verbatim in Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with the header and multiple NACo experience bullets; use “communications” instead of “messaging” for a more senior tone.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it’s too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and recent strengths rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems design • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they are important for target roles; otherwise trim to avoid diluting recent enterprise CMS experience.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems design” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- Use “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “AI-enabled search experiences” for sharper, outcome-oriented wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform names in both sections.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and recent consulting bullets, so keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Tighten it around analysis, reporting, and optimization outcomes, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for KPI development, executive reporting, SEO analysis, and performance insights.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-support reporting” for clearer business impact.
- Change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and content performance analysis” if accurate; it better reflects Clarity and broader optimization work.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase such as “used to guide content, UX, and platform decisions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet about expanding analytics infrastructure; keep this item tool/capability-focused rather than repeating accomplishments.
- Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already evidenced in recent experience, so avoid overloading this line with extra explanation.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and with tool-level detail in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value operational scope rather than generic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability summary: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio leadership in recent roles.
- Consider swapping “Studio operations” for “Studio buildout and operations” only if you want to signal the NACo studio achievement more explicitly.
- Keep terms parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad formats (“hybrid and virtual event production”) with narrow tools unless each adds distinct value.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies’ “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- Tool-specific detail here overlaps with Technical + IT (“Premiere Pro,” “Livestream studio workflows,” “Podcast production”).

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to a lower-priority item or remove if not materially used in recent roles.
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency.
- If you want stronger impact, align with work history: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the fuller version in one place and shorten the other.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel redundant given GitHub Actions/technical tools unless it supports a notable project.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity and consistency: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • REST/API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers unless they matter technically; “HTML5/CSS3” adds little value on a leadership CV.
- Consider grouping by function for faster scanning: “Front-end: HTML/CSS, JavaScript/jQuery | Integration & deployment: APIs, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions | Tagging: Google Tag Manager”
- If accurate, add one higher-impact qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “for Drupal implementations, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so keep this item focused on hands-on technical implementation tools.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a generic tool dump. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills, so it should emphasize systems-building tools over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to highlight automation/platform tools first: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move general collaboration tools out unless they are true differentiators; if kept, place last: “Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp”
- Consider renaming the category to be more precise: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie these tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing all equally, e.g., “Built editorial planning and cross-team workflow systems in Airtable, Jira, and Asana”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so repeating them here without added specificity is redundant.
- Slack/Teams overlap more with collaboration than technical systems; they may dilute the section.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and audience-engagement systems rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of just tools: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign deployment**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it to keep the list stronger and more current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with multiple work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid adding generic “email campaigns” language here unless you specify platform-specific capabilities.
- “Engagement” may also overlap with Core Competencies; use this item for concrete systems, not broad communications skills.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this line is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, make it tighter and more implementation-focused rather than repeating broad capability labels.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Replace vague terms like **Dashboarding** with a clearer output such as **KPI reporting** or **executive dashboards**.
- Consider swapping **SEO** for **Google Search Console** or **technical SEO analysis** to make the skill more concrete and tool-based.
- If space allows elsewhere, move outcomes like “expanded analytics infrastructure” and reporting impact to recent NACo/consulting bullets rather than this skills list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping the stronger version in one place only.
- **Looker Studio / Power BI / dashboarding** also echo the NACo achievement bullet; avoid repeating all three in multiple sections.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with 1–2 concrete outputs or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add specific contributions and scope: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring weekly video updates for member communications and advocacy.”
- Tighten leadership phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “coordinated/delegated work for a digital media associate” unless you formally supervised.
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience reach, event size, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; in this item, position it as launching or early production support.
- Avoid repeating broad “web, email, social, video” leadership language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to” with stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “supported,” depending on actual ownership.
- If possible, add one concrete output or scope metric: number of episodes, audiences served, or types of projects/materials produced.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing that repeats later roles focused on web, video, email and social leadership.
- Don’t overstate multimedia leadership here; later entries already show progression into full digital/media ownership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and multiple work bullets. Make it more tool-specific and current, emphasizing software proficiency rather than broad production capabilities already proven elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software & Audio/Video Tools**
- Replace broad phrases with tool-led wording: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator**
- If accurate, sharpen the last two items to: **Livestream production systems** • **Podcast editing and production**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recent relevance: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Livestream production systems • Photoshop • Illustrator • Podcast editing and production**
